definition.note: No closed form is stored for this surface. It is defined by its shipped implementation in math_art.minsurf.parametric, which is authoritative; an unverified transcription would silently define a different surface.

provenance.definition: Derived from the Math Art generator registries and cross-referenced to the literature; not transcribed from any gallery's compilation.
sources: B. Riemann, 'Uber die Flache vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', Abh. Konigl. Ges. Wiss. Gottingen 13 (1867), posthumous.
B. Riemann, 'Ueber die Flaeche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung', Abh. Koenigl. Ges. Wiss. Goettingen 13 (1867) 3-52.

W. H. Meeks III, J. Perez, A. Ros, 'Properly embedded minimal planar domains', Ann. of Math. 181 (2015) 473-546 -- any properly embedded minimal surface of genus 0 is the plane, catenoid, helicoid, or a Riemann example.

cross_checked.detail: page title 'Skew catenoid' vs record name "Riemann's Minimal Example"
record year 1867, page says 1860 -- recorded as a disagreement rather than reconciled; sources differ on when the surface was first studied

caveats: Foliated by circles and lines in parallel planes; Meeks, Perez and Ros later proved it is the only such properly embedded singly periodic example of genus zero.
